chain.label: FAA surveillance of Fine Air cargo operations inadequate
chain.trigger: the failure of the FAA to adequately monitor Fine Air's operational control responsibilities for cargo loading and the failure of the FAA to ensure that known cargo-related deficiencies were corrected

chain.label: Fine Air failed to exercise operational control over the cargo loading process
chain.trigger: Fine Air managers stated that before the accident, the company did not supervise loading operations carried out by Aeromar

chain.label: Cargo loaders and loading supervisor untrained in weight-and-balance consequences
chain.trigger: the loaders who loaded the accident airplane were not aware of the potentially catastrophic consequences of misloading the airplane and the failing to properly secure cargo

caused_by.evidence: Air carriers are currently not required to provide initial classroom training or recurrent training for personnel involved in cargo handling
Training for loading personnel at Aeromar and Fine Air was described as on-the-job training

chain.label: Erroneous load sheet and revised weight distribution form never reaching the loaders
chain.trigger: procedures used by Fine Air and Aeromar to prepare and distribute cargo weight pallet distribution forms and final weight and balance load sheets were inadequate to ensure that these documents correctly reflected the true loading of the accident airplane

caused_by.evidence: Fine Air did not weigh palletized cargo delivered by Aeromar or have other procedures in place to verify cargo weights and the accuracy of the load form provided to the crew

chain.label: Loaders pushed 13 pallets aft one position and turned pallet 4 90 degrees, matching neither load plan
chain.trigger: all pallets from position 5 aft were pushed back one position each, which resulted in pallet position 17 being filled and position 5 being emptied. Pallet 4 was turned 90 degrees and pushed back

caused_by.evidence: the security guard was not aware of the airplane change, and that he instructed Aeromar loaders to load the airplane in accordance with the weight distribution form he possessed for N30UA
loaders did not recognize the importance of loading an airplane consistent with the calculated weight and balance plan
Little or no attempt was made to determine whether these changes would adversely affect the airplane in flight

chain.label: Pallet locks left unengaged; cargo not restrained
chain.trigger: 57 of the 60 locks recovered from the wreckage (from a total of 85 installed) were found in the unlocked position

caused_by.evidence: he did not verify that they had been latched, relying instead on the thoroughness of loaders
the Aeromar cargo loading supervisor failed to confirm that the cargo was properly restrained

chain.label: CG near or aft of the aft limit (about 32.8 percent MAC) with cargo heavier than manifested
chain.trigger: the CG of the accident airplane was near or even aft of the airplane's aft CG limit

caused_by.evidence: pushing the 13 pallets aft shifted the CG farther aft by at least 8 percent MAC
the weight of the cargo that Aeromar provided to Fine Air could have been 5,196 pounds more than listed on the pallet weight form

chain.label: Stabilizer trim set 2.4 units ANU, mis-set by at least 1.5 units for the actual CG
chain.trigger: the CG shift resulted in the airplane's trim being mis-set by at least 1.5 units ANU (2.4 minus 0.9 units at 94,119 pounds)

caused_by.evidence: the airplane being misloaded to produce a more aft center of gravity and a correspondingly incorrect stabilizer trim setting
the stabilizer trim was set during taxi-out at 2.4 units ANU, the value appropriate for the trim setting and CG of 30 percent MAC that the flightcrew had been given

chain.label: Extreme uncommanded nose-up pitch at rotation
chain.trigger: about 16 seconds after the start of rotation ... the airplane reached an extremely nose-high pitch attitude in the range of 30 degrees and an AOA approaching 20 degrees

caused_by.evidence: Such a mistrim would cause a greater than expected nose-up pitching moment
This would be exacerbated by the lighter control column forces that result from an aft CG location
cargo compression or shifting might have exacerbated the pitch-up moment as the pitch increased

chain.label: Continued aft column input and 5-second delay before nose-down trim
chain.trigger: The first officer's continued aft column input for 2 seconds after the captain began his 'easy, easy, easy, easy' remark exacerbated the pitch up that was developing from the mistrimmed stabilizer

caused_by.evidence: about a 5-second delay occurred between the flightcrew's first attempt to control the pitch up with nose-down column inputs and the first inputs of nose-down trim

chain.label: Aerodynamic stall, brief recovery, then second stall
chain.trigger: the airplane pitched up quickly into a stall, that it recovered briefly from the stall, that it stalled again, and that recovery before ground impact was unlikely once the stall series began

caused_by.evidence: an AOA approaching 20 degrees, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall (an AOA of 15 degrees was sufficient to bring the airplane into the stall region)

If the first officer had chosen to trim the airplane in the first, critical moments during and after rotation ... might have been able to correct most, or all, of the mistrim condition, preventing the airplane from stalling

chain.label: Stall entered at about 300 feet just after liftoff
chain.trigger: about 16 seconds after the start of rotation, at an altitude of about 300 feet msl, the airplane reached an extremely nose-high pitch attitude

chain.label: Uncontrolled impact with terrain about 3,000 feet west of runway 27R and postcrash fire
chain.trigger: Ground scars and wreckage scatter indicated that the airplane impacted terrain in a tail first, right wing down attitude

caused_by.evidence: This resulted in an AOA of at least 49 degrees at the time of impact, consistent with the airplane being in a deep stall
once the initial stall was reached, full recovery was unlikely because of the airplane's low altitude and the airplane's rapidly decreasing performance

chain.label: Five fatalities; airplane destroyed
chain.trigger: The three flightcrew members and one security guard on board were killed, and a motorist was killed on the ground

caused_by.evidence: The airplane was destroyed by impact and a postcrash fire ... The accident was not survivable
